sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Chamunda Electrical Limited, CHAMUNDA, NSE Emerge listed 11 February 2025 per audited results and decoded official master. Traded SM series eligible; price-discovery status is not suspension. Audited capital ₹11.0046 crore at ₹10 implies 11,004,600 shares; master 11,004,594 differs by six shares, immaterial to valuation but primary audited capital used. Review cutoff 20 October 2026; the official ₹41 close is dated 19 October, not a live quote. Statements are standalone Indian Accounting Standards. FY25 annual report, final February 2025 prospectus and FY26 audited results were read. The issuer IR page and exchange cache did not yield a FY26 full annual report, limiting current deposit/debt/RPT detail. All four gates are Conditional rather than automatic failures.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: Canonical factors are GOV 4, MOAT 4, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP 4, CASH 2, BAL 6, EXEC 5 and EARN 4. R remains NS; D 3, P 4 and L 1 remain independently scoreable. Exact weights, coverage and unrenormalized bounds are retained. Persistent CASH 2 caps Growth Quality GQS at 5; it does not automatically cap BQS or prove unfinanceability. Low expected-return confidence does not erase supported quality factors, and thin trading is not confused with a suspension.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: The business operates and maintains substations up to 66 kV, tests and commissions up to 220 kV and operates a 1.5 MW solar park. EHV erection, control wiring, earthing and related works complement maintenance. Skilled field labor and contract compliance drive delivery; FY26 payroll ₹21.199 crore was 66.16% of sales. The direct-cost bill also rose to ₹5.3963 crore from ₹2.2347 crore. This is not a scalable software-like margin model: new sites require staff, supervision, payroll funding and receivable collection.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Longstanding GETCO access and technical experience make qualification and delivery capability valuable. The largest customer supplied 82.48% of FY24 revenue and 70.67% in the nine months to December 2024, however, so tender renewals and customer terms can dominate economics. These historical percentages are not claimed as FY26 mix. Techno Electric’s primary FY26 group statements show₹3,251.63 crore sales,₹473.87 crore owner PAT and− ₹589.96 crore CFO, illustrating the sector’s potential working-capital intensity. Its large EPC, AMI and data-center mix differs materially; no direct peer P/E or automatic premium is imported.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Restated FY22/FY23/FY24 sales were ₹11.2331/₹13.9424/₹19.9493 crore, followed by FY25 ₹25.2857 and FY26 ₹32.0401 crore. Four-year CAGR 29.96% and three-year 31.96% support REV 8 under the short-history cap. FY22 restated PAT was a ₹0.5128 crore loss, FY23₹0.3121 and FY24₹2.4363; these must not be mixed indiscriminately with statutory PAT. FY26 H2 sales ₹15.4567 crore were below H1 ₹16.5834 crore; H2 PAT ₹1.2607 crore was below H1 ₹2.2563 crore, with H1 benefiting from the prior-tax release. Annual growth alone therefore overstates recent profit momentum.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: The April 1 disclosure covers 88 GETCO substations for 36 months with₹63.47 crore including 18% GST. Excluding GST gives ₹53.7881 crore, an illustrative₹17.9294 crore annually if evenly spread. This is not automatically incremental to existing contracts; commencement, replacements and billing milestones remain unverified. October 17’s Vapi order is ₹1.6851 crore including GST, or₹1.4280 crore ex GST, over 8 months from commencement. The model does not add either gross order mechanically to revenue. March CWIP ₹4.6556 crore and unspent IPO testing-kit allocation₹0.8007 crore show that capital deployment and return realization still matter. Existing CWIP is not paid twice in the model.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: FY25 director remuneration₹0.165 crore was modest relative to profit, but related-party operating flows need monitoring. Vendor advances to Chamunda Electrotech and Chamunda Solar totalled₹1.9303 crore, alongside ₹1.2175 crore service purchases from Electrotech. Historical demand-loan schedules noted unavailable written agreements; FY25 related-party debt was only ₹0.0244 crore after repayment, so large historical flows are not treated as current debt. The prospectus explicitly reconciles historical depreciation, gratuity, tax and period-allocation corrections, including a reduction of FY23 PAT from ₹0.8456 crore to ₹0.3121 crore. This is a disclosed controls concern, not evidence that all current figures are unusable or proof of misconduct. Full FY26 related-party notes and current repayment terms remain to be obtained.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text: FY26 PBT ₹4.2204 crore fell from ₹4.4954 crore after prior items; against FY25 pre-prior-item PBT ₹5.1026 crore the decline was 17.29%. Reported PAT ₹3.517 crore includes a ₹0.4399 crore prior-tax provision release. Removing that release gives ₹3.0771 crore; further removing₹0.4153 crore other income at an assumed 25% tax gives an analytical₹2.7656 crore proxy. Core EBITDA is ₹4.825 crore. CFO ₹0.0162 crore less cash capex ₹3.2694 crore gives FCF− ₹3.2532 crore; receivables, advances and other assets absorbed ₹1.7677/₹1.4801/₹0.7463 crore. Borrowings supplied₹2.6991 crore. FY24 statutory versus restated CFO differs₹0.2187 crore, offset exactly by CFI− ₹0.1637 and CFF− ₹0.0550, leaving cash movement unchanged. There is no missing-cash allegation. March cash is ₹0.9392 crore, distinct from ₹9.1013 crore other noncurrent assets. Prior-year deposits and physical cash are not presumed available today; unspent IPO ₹0.8007 crore remains earmarked.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
Model correction — 20 October 2026: The opening-claim treatment in our earlier scenario calculations was incomplete. This revision explicitly bridges identified current settlements, retained net noncurrent claims and uncertain-composition sensitivities. The updated model replaces the earlier scenario version; the companies’ historical financial figures and published accounts have not changed.

At ₹41 and 11,004,600 shares, market value is ₹45.11886 crore: 12.83× reported PAT or 16.31× the normalized proxy. No unverified deposit surplus is netted from enterprise value. The linked five-year bear/base/bull models assume growth 5%/14%/22%, margins 11%/15%/18%, NWC 50%/40%/35% and exit EV/EBITDA 6/9/12. Every year funds payroll economics through margin, tax, NWC, maintenance capex and project completion before debt/cash changes. Half-year interest on new draws is solved jointly with tax; ordinary repayments occur at year-end. Terminal prices ₹23.59/₹82.01/₹182.64 imply conditional annual returns −10.46%/14.87%/34.82%, not expected return estimates. Base completion budget ₹2 crore beyond IPO kit is an explicit assumption; unverified deposit availability and award incrementality keep R NS. The reference cases do not settle the unresolved ₹1.7811 crore current-provision balance; this is an incomplete timing assumption, not a zero-liability conclusion. The separate fully funded sensitivity pays the entire balance once in FY27, without asserting that all of it is income tax. The FY26 balance sheet reports no separate noncurrent provision or other noncurrent liability to add; no older gratuity balance is imposed again. Reference bear/base/bull prices are ₹23.5916/₹82.0120/₹182.6422, with annual returns -10.4646%/14.8732%/34.8228%. Full-current-provision-settlement prices are ₹21.2023/₹80.0853/₹180.9712, with returns -12.3565%/14.3283%/34.5752%. Normal liabilities already deducted in opening WC are not paid twice.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: Losing or repricing the dominant utility relationship can leave payroll and site costs before receivables collect. Related-vendor advances, unfinished CWIP and restricted deposits can immobilize apparent balance-sheet strength. Severe demand/margin, 60% NWC, 15% funding cost,₹6 crore additional completion and unavailable IPO reserve are modeled together; a ₹1.9303 crore advance-loss proxy is tested separately and in severe stress, not asserted actual impairment. The FY25 note reports a ₹0.5429 crore income-tax contingency associated with an appealed AY 2017–18 assessment; the ₹0.2928 crore net notice reflects adjustment of a ₹0.2501 crore refund, not a second additive claim. The earlier GST demand was reduced to ₹0.0079 crore, provided and paid. Ordinary disputed tax amounts are not treated as misconduct. New borrowing outputs are requirements, not proof a bank will lend. With the opening-claim convention, the severe case requires peak modeled debt of ₹14.7464 crore, terminal price ₹0.0000 and annual return -100.0000%. These are conditional funding requirements, not evidence of committed facilities. Paying the whole unresolved current provision increases severe peak debt to ₹18.2391 crore. That bound is separate from any contingent disputed-tax stress already modeled.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Fivefold and tenfold market values are approximately ₹225.59 crore and ₹451.19 crore. At an illustrative 15× P/E and 9% net margin, they require ₹167.11 crore and ₹334.21 crore sales before debt/cash adjustment, versus ₹32.04 crore now. Those imply about 39% and 60% annual sales growth over five years, well above the base case and requiring much broader staffed capacity and funding. The present 36-month award is not enough to establish that path. Dilution, working capital and customer concentration may prevent business growth translating into equivalent per-share growth.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Obtain FY26 full annual notes for debt terms, deposit liens/maturities, cash composition, advances, receivable ageing and related-party balances. Verify GETCO commencement, replacement versus incremental scope, site handover and collection milestones. Reconcile CWIP commissioning with the remaining testing-kit allocation and actual completion budget. Demand sustained improvement in CFO/PAT rather than merely sales growth; monitor half-year margin excluding tax releases. Market review: 36 observations within 60 sessions imply 38.46 exit days at 5% participation even before missing days; the 24 gaps are not asserted zero. One 3,000-share lot costs ₹123000. REG1 flags fewer than 100 PANs and irregular SME trading. Live depth, circuits and feasible position size need verification independently of the quote.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Completed deep review, conditional hold for investment purposes. Supported quality scores remain available, but cash conversion, capital deployment and concentration prevent a high-quality growth conclusion. IAS is NS because the funded operating scenarios are conditional on unresolved material inputs, not because the model was omitted. A numerical L 1 is justified by observed turnover alone; G4 failure is not established. Reassessment requires collections, deposit/funding clarity, budgeted commissioning and execution evidence rather than a price-only trigger.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: The source ledger distinguishes FY25 annual notes, FY26 audited results, the final February 2025 prospectus, two GETCO awards, issuer IR availability checks, official dated quotes/master/REG1 and a primary economic comparator. Original latest financial pages and historical restatement layout were visually inspected to avoid OCR-driven allegations. The linked annual model contains funding, interest and tax calculations, terminal equity, completion-budget, collection, margin, deposit, loss and dilution sensitivities, and 15% entry hurdles. FY26 complete annual notes remain unavailable; no invented current composition substitutes for them. The opening-claim reconciliation distinguishes current cash settlements, normal operating liabilities already in working capital, net noncurrent employee/deposit claims retained at exit, and uncertain composition bounds. March balances are not asserted to remain outstanding in October. No immediate payment of all noncurrent provisions is assumed.

GOV.reason: Disclosed historical accounting corrections and material related-vendor advances demand oversight; modest remuneration and explicit restatement/tax disclosure are counterevidence. Neither a normal tax appeal nor a corrected item proves misconduct.

MOAT.reason: Substation experience and renewed GETCOaccess support competence; dominant customer, tender pricing and labor-heavy delivery constrain pricing power. Larger EPC peers are not equivalent franchises.

REV.reason: Four-year revenue CAGR29.96% and three-year31.96% support8under limited-historycap. Aprilaward supports runway but overlaps/replacement unknown; no grossaward added directly to sales.

DUR.reason: Essential maintenance and36 monthaward provide recurrence; customer concentration and tender renewals limit durability beyond the contract.

CAP.reason: Newtestingkit may expand capability and debt/equity modest; growing CWIP and related-vendor advances tie capital while completion returns are not yet demonstrated.

CASH.reason: Lateststatutory CFO1.5341/0.5679/0.0162 crore versus positive profits shows persistent weak conversion; latest FCF−3.2532 crore. Earlier restated FY23 cash2.0963 is positive counterevidence, not enough to erase deterioration.

BAL.reason: Debt2.7235 versus equity28.6015 is modest and historical deposits meaningful; actualfreecash0.9392, new borrowing and deposit restrictions limit strength. No unverified NCA treated as freely nettable cash.

EXEC.reason: Sales growth and new GETCOawards evidence execution; lower core profit and slowtestingkit/CWIP deployment temper this. Commissioning and collections remain unverified.

EARN.reason: FY26 tax release0.4399 and otherincome0.4153 support reported PAT while PBT falls; historical corrections constrain cleantrend. Auditedresults and explicit bridge permit analysis rather than blanket NS.

R.reason: Annual funded scenarios are complete but FY26 deposit/debt terms, completion budget and award incrementality prevent a sufficiently supported expected-return band.

D.reason: Low opening leverage offsets some risk; customerloss, fixed payroll, slow collections and extremelythin exit create permanent-loss pathways. Severe funding is a requirement, not provenavailable.

P.reason: Datedmarket value₹45.11886 crore is about12.83×reported PAT and16.31×normalizedproxy; valuation is not obviously expensive, but uncertainfree FD and margincash conversion prevent a high mispricing score.

L.reason: Observed-onlyexit38.46 days already exceeds20 daylowestband, robust without zero-fill.3000 sharelot₹123000,3latesttrades and exchange PAN/irregular-tradingflags reinforce this. It does not establish outrightuntradeability.

gates.reason: Historical corrections and related-vendor advances require monitoring; no independently established integrity failure. Ordinary sourced tax appeal is not misconduct.

The original latest profit-and-loss, balance-sheet and cash-flow statements are readable and reconcilable. FY24 statutory and restated cash-flow changes offset, with no missing cash. Full FY26 notes remain unavailable, leaving related-party and fixed-deposit details uncertain; this is not a universal critical reliability hold.

Opening debt is modest, but free cash flow is negative, advances tie up funds and the completion budget is unknown. The linked model explicitly borrows when necessary; committed facility headroom and deposit release must be verified. Unfinanceability has not been proved.

Dated SM-series trades are verified, but the observed-only exit estimate is extremely slow. Missing days are not automatically zero-volume sessions. Live depth and blanket surveillance clearance are unavailable. L 1 is not proof of a G4 failure.
